findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed no hand sink available at the stand. The PIC was informed and was unaware of the requirement. A neighboring stand volunteered to share their hand sink for the duration of the event. Ensure a hand sink with a free-flowing spigot is available and equipped with soap, paper towel, and a catch bucket.
findings.citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following storage order violations on the facility:
1. Raw chicken stored above cooked beef barbacoa and carrots
2. Packaged raw whole chickens stored on top of packaged butter and above raw beef
3. Raw beef stored above celery 

The PIC was informed of proper storage order guidelines and the cooler was rearranged. The inspector provided a storage order flyer for staff education.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed scented bleach in use for food-contact sanitizing. The PIC was informed of chemical requirements for food contact surfaces. Proper bleach was available on site. The sanitizer bucket was emptied and refilled with proper chemical. Ensure staff are using unscented, plain bleach with a valid EPA-registered label for sanitizing food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
findings.comment: Inspector observed shell eggs stored on the counter with no time as a public health control label indicating discard time. The PIC was informed and labels were added to each flat of eggs. Ensure staff are marking cartons with the time they are removed from the cooler and using or discarding within four hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a bag of onions, canned cheese, and single service items stored directly on the ground in the dry storage area. The PIC was informed and plans to acquire pallets or crates to elevate the food items from the floor. Ensure all food items are stored at least 6 inches off the ground prior to the next routine inspection. 

Inspector observed no splash guard present between the sods syrup boxes and the mop sink. The shelf of syrups is located right next to the mop sink, risking splash contamination of the syrup boxes from the mop water. Ensure a splash guard is installed prior to the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the head of the mop stored directly in the basin of the mop sink. The PIC was informed and the mop was inverted. Ensure staff are storing the mop in the manner that allows for proper drip drying.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
